final_message:
Fixed. `postSlug("Crème brûlée recipes")` now returns `creme-brulee-recipes`, and `npm test` passes all 3 tests, including `test/blog-slug.test.js`.

The cause was the vendored `slugify` in `vendor/slugify/index.js`. It deletes every character outside `a-z0-9`, so `è` and `û` disappeared rather than turning into `e` and `u`. Since `vendor/` is off-limits, I changed `src/blog/slug.js` instead. It decomposes accents (NFD) and strips the combining marks before calling the vendored function.

Not changed:
- `src/shop/product-url.js` also calls the same vendored `slugify`, so product URLs with accents still lose those letters. You asked only about blog posts, so I left it alone. The same one-line fix would apply there if you want it.
- The fix lives in our code, so an upstream `slugify` upgrade won't affect it.

I didn't commit anything.
